x: Ian Wells has been the Civil Service 400mH champion for the last 4 years. He has joined Belgrave to increase his opportunities for top class competition which is limited in the Great Yarmouth area.

But perhaps the most gratifying moment was seeing Ian Wells gain his 400 metre hurdles place on merit. A team manager's dream - always turning up and covering a whole range of events having scored many points at his specialist events.

Ian Wells worked hard for his 3rd spot in the 400 hurdles and Stuart Paton came from last to second in the 800m over the last 60m. Meanwhile Phil Spivey gained 2nd in the hammer (thankful that he was eligible for the Cup) and Chris Symonds threw a lifetime best also to gain 2nd in the shot.
Jon Ridgeon gained a fine second to carry on his gruelling race schedule over the high hurdles while Ian Wells again stepped in to pip Dalton Grant (yes - Dalton Grant!) in the 'B' hurdles.
First place in the 'B' 400m hurdles for Ian Wells gave us a winning start to the afternoon.

The track started off in sparkling fashion with Paul Beaumont starting slowly but gaining all the way round to clinch victory in the 'A' 400 hurdles while Ian Wells went off like a man possessed to hang on well for his first Division 1 victory.
